newsitem.title: USA: Zebra says issue of control ended merger talks.
newsitem.headline: Zebra says issue of control ended merger talks.

text.p: A proposed merger of Zebra Technologies Corp and Eltron International Inc fell through because of concerns over who would control the combined company, Zebra said Thursday.
"One of the primary concerns that emerged was corporate governance," Ed Kaplan, chairman and chief executive officer of Zebra, told analysts in a conference call. "Another concern was CEO authority."
Last month, the two bar code technology companies said they signed a letter of intent to merge in a stock swap, but they said late Wednesday they had terminated talks.

Kaplan said the company at this point does not have another merger or acquisition in the works, but does have about $86 million in cash, putting it in an "excellent position" to pursue other opportunities should they arise.

Under the agreement with Eltron, Kaplan would have served as chairman of the combined company and Donald Skinner, Eltron's chairman and chief executive, would have become president and chief executive.
"I intended to operate as an active chairman," Kaplan said, adding that he would have focussed on company strategy and board issues.
"Essentially, negotiations moved in the direction of Ed Kaplan becoming a quarterly chairman, and frankly that was simply not acceptable," Kaplan said.

In addition, four Zebra board members were to join the new board, compared with three of Eltron's. Kaplan said Zebra has nearly twice the sales and about three times the net income of Eltron, and two founding shareholders own nearly 30 percent of Zebra.
"As discussions continued Eltron became uncomfortable with the four-to-three provision," Kaplan said. "We never reached the due diligence stage, so due diligence was not the issue."
Zebra will take a charge of about $200,000 in the fourth quarter from expenses incurred with the merger. He said the company also put a hold on some developments during the negotiations.
"There were a couple of areas of the company that we put a halt on some things that we were doing," Kaplan said, estimating this cost the company about 30 days or fewer.

"It was one of the reasons why we were pushing for conclusion here, because the clock was ticking," Kaplan said. "It was affecting some of our individual efforts, especially because we are in the planning process now for fiscal '97."

Zebra will continue its expansion into the lower-end bar code printer market. Kaplan said the company unveiled two printers, priced at $595 and $795, at a trade show two weeks ago, and orders are better than expected.

Kaplan said he will continue as chairman and chief executive of Zebra. Under the merger agreement, he said he had not expected the chairman position to be full-time and was planning to pursue other areas of interest.

"(I)'m very interested in the long-term future of this business, I definitely expect to continue to do what it is that I've been doing," Kaplan said. "We will certainly be sorting things out here in terms of what our options are, but that's my expectation there."
Shares of Zebra fell 5-3/8 at 24-5/8 and Eltron traded 5-1/2 lower at 32-3/4.
